issues.description:
Method return type mismatch for Farm.singFarmSong() and its helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal):
- Problem statement UML (problem_statement.md line 20) and the template implementation (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) declare/expect singFarmSong() and singFarmSongVerse(Animal) to be void methods that print the song (the template provides a void singFarmSong() and a void singFarmSongVerse(...) that prints). 
- The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) defines private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal) and public String singFarmSong(), returning the song text as a String instead of printing it.
This inconsistency (void/printing vs String/returning) is structural: the same method names have different return types across artifacts. It can confuse students which signature to implement and whether tests expect printed output or a returned String, and may lead to compilation or test mismatches depending on the expected API.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the API consistent across all artifacts. Two options (choose one and apply across problem statement, template, and solution):
1) Follow the UML/problem description: change the solution methods to printing void methods. Update solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java so singFarmSong() is public void and singFarmSongVerse(Animal) is private void and both print the verses (using System.out.println). Adjust any tests to expect printed output.
2) Or adopt the solution's approach: update the problem statement UML and the template to declare singFarmSong(): String and singFarmSongVerse(Animal): String and document that the method returns the full verse/song text (then update the template Farm.java signature/comments accordingly). Ensure tests and README reflect returning a String rather than printing.
Apply the chosen change to all three artifacts (problem statement, template, solution) so students have a single, unambiguous expected signature and behavior.
